prompt: Photorealistic interior of a medieval 14th-century harbourmaster's office in a Hanseatic port town, at eye level. A dim, dark room: heavy soot-blackened oak ceiling beams, rough stone walls with patchy flaking lime plaster, worn wide oak floorboards, deep-set window with small leaded diamond-shaped panes in thick stone, one casement swung open. Outside the window a bright foggy morning: pale grey fog with faint silhouettes of tall wooden ship masts, yards and rigging. Cold daylight from the window is the main light, the rest of the room falls into deep shadow. Seen from just inside the door, looking straight at the window across the room. A heavy oak desk under the window with ledgers, a quill and inkwell, wax seals, a rolled sea chart and one guttering tallow candle. An iron-banded sea chest, coiled hemp rope, a hanging iron lantern, a brass astrolabe on a shelf. Dust drifting in the beam of light. Moody chiaroscuro, realistic aged materials, cinematic 35mm photograph, no people.
